solutions.check: 30 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 29 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Stop girl coming out to car topless

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a girl making her formal entry into society

indicators.note: without its top, so the first letter of the word car is dropped

explanation.surface: A girl tells someone to stop leaving the house for a convertible with the roof down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' is not leaving but a debutante's first appearance in society.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar someone is to prevent or bar them, a synonym of stop.

clue.text: Paid, as per arrangement, to clear off

indicators.note: an arrangement here means the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is paid, as agreed, to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear is to vanish or depart, as when told to clear off.

clue.text: Goose found in part of London

explanation.surface: A goose is discovered in a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Brent is a borough of north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: The brent is a small dark wild goose; Brent is a London borough.

clue.text: Take over from old magistrate — he's about fifty-one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the magistrate goes round the Roman numerals

parts.note: a reeve was a medieval local official or magistrate
LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone replaces an ageing magistrate who is around fifty-one years old.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to take their place on duty.

clue.text: Hormone makes Alan and Enid run amok

indicators.note: running amok means going wild, so the letters of the names and R are thrown into disorder

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Two people, Alan and Enid, go wild, as if fired up by a rush of hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run amok' looks like one phrase, but 'run' gives R to the fodder and 'amok' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenalin is the hormone released by the adrenal glands in stress.

clue.text: Land with Felix in the south of the peninsula

definitions.text: Land with Felix in the south of the peninsula

parts.words: Land with Felix in the south of the peninsula
parts.note: the classical name for the fertile south-west of the great peninsula paired the land's name with Felix, meaning happy

explanation.surface: A country holds a man named Felix in its southern region.
explanation.walkthrough: Felix looks like a man (or the cartoon cat), but Arabia Felix was the Roman name for the southern part of the peninsula, roughly Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula between the Red Sea and the Gulf is this land, whose south the Romans called Felix.

clue.text: Assign new limits to Communist east — splendid!

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist
E is the compass abbreviation for east
fine means excellent or splendid

explanation.surface: A communist delighted with the eastern bloc approves new borders.
explanation.definitionFit: To redefine is to set fresh boundaries or terms for something.

clue.text: River has risen about 45 inches? What a story!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the river goes round the measure
has risen, in a down clue, says the river's letters are read upwards

parts.note: the Avon is an English river
an ell is an old cloth measure of 45 inches

explanation.surface: A river floods by about forty-five inches, and someone exclaims at the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has risen' turns AVON into NOVA, which goes 'about' ELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, a tale longer than a short story.

clue.text: Feature of policy meant to be altered

parts.note: a party line is its policy

indicators.note: to be altered says the letters of meant are changed into another order

explanation.surface: Some part of a policy was intended to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be altered' rearranges MEANT into AMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineament is a distinctive feature, especially of the face.

clue.text: Refusal to include Peter, for example, is objectionable

indicators.note: to include means the refusal surrounds the saint

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, a refusal
Peter is a saint, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: Turning down someone called Peter is thought offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means unpleasant or offensive.

clue.text: Plagiarism forbidden, say, to percussion group

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase only has to sound right when spoken

parts.note: plagiarism is to steal another's work; forbidden is banned

explanation.surface: A drummers' ensemble is warned that copying other people's music is not allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel band is a Caribbean ensemble playing tuned oil-drum percussion instruments.

clue.text: Given usual part as goddess?

indicators.note: part says the letters are a portion carried within the words Given usual

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being cast in her usual stage role makes an actress a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the Roman deity of love.

clue.text: Anthropomorphism is a sad error

parts.note: pathetic means sad or pitiful
a fallacy is a mistaken belief or error

explanation.surface: Someone claims that attributing human traits to things is a regrettable mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruskin's term for ascribing human feelings to nature, a kind of personification of the non-human.

clue.text: Pass late EEC return to Deputy Leader

parts.note: ex means former, which is one sense of late

indicators.note: return says the letters of EEC are read backwards
the leader of the word Deputy is its first letter

explanation.surface: A deputy leader hands back an old European Economic Community document after it expired.
explanation.walkthrough: The EEC was the European Economic Community, forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed is to go beyond or surpass, a sense of pass.

clue.text: Chambers offering strong defence — for co-respondents?

explanation.surface: Fortified rooms are recommended to people named in a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: Casemates are armoured gun chambers in a fortress; co-respondents named in a divorce case are, playfully, 'case mates'.
explanation.definitionFit: Armoured vaults in a fort are casemates; people named together in one lawsuit are jokily partners in the same case.

clue.text: In Confederate state reds scattered foreign assailants

parts.note: Virginia, abbreviated VA, was one of the US Confederate states

indicators.note: scattered means the letters of reds are spread about in new order

explanation.surface: In the American South, communists are dispersed by attackers from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Invaders are attackers who enter a country from outside.

clue.text: Potsdam palace carelessly named

explanation.surface: A royal palace near Berlin is given its name without much thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederick the Great's summer palace at Potsdam bears a French name meaning 'without worry'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means without care, and it is also the name of Frederick the Great's palace.

clue.text: Stoic air unusual for a Judas

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of Stoic air are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A stoic manner is unusual for a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so a Judas is any traitor.

clue.text: Partner's reaction in tricky contest

parts.note: in bridge, a game of tricks, the partner's reply to an opening bid has a technical name

explanation.surface: A partner reacts during a difficult competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky contest' is bridge, a card game won by taking tricks; the partner's reply to an opening bid is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply or reaction is a response, and in bridge it is the technical term for partner's answering bid.

clue.text: There's nothing to replace silk in protective clothing!

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: to replace means the letters of silk are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that nothing could substitute for silk in protective garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' rearranges SILK into ILSK, set between O and IN; 'in' looks like a link word before the definition but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilskins are waterproof garments of oiled cloth.

clue.text: Petty officer going about to make US port

indicators.note: going about means surrounding, so the petty officer is wrapped round the word to

parts.note: bosn is a variant spelling of bosun, the ship's petty officer

explanation.surface: A naval petty officer turns his ship around to reach an American harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Boston is a major Massachusetts seaport.

clue.text: Threatening order in Oxford University Society

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
OUS abbreviates Oxford University Society

explanation.surface: A menacing decree is issued in an Oxford college club.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means boding ill or menacing.

clue.text: Crustacean lives up-river, round beginning of December

parts.note: is means exists or lives

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the river's letters are read upwards

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the beginning of the word December is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shellfish lives upstream near the start of December.
explanation.definitionFit: Isopods, such as woodlice, are a group of crustaceans.

clue.text: Scotch or Irish assistants for spelling expert?

explanation.surface: Someone asks which whisky a wizard's helpers prefer.
explanation.walkthrough: First the phrase read literally: whiskies everybody knows. Then the witch's demon helpers; a 'spelling expert' is someone who casts spells, not a speller.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch and Irish are well-known whiskies, while demons serving a witch are her familiars.

clue.text: Marvellous engineer turned into hymn-writer

parts.note: fab is short for fabulous, marvellous

indicators.note: turned says the engineer's letters are reversed

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of military engineers

explanation.surface: A brilliant engineer changed into a composer of hymns.
explanation.walkthrough: F. W. Faber was a Victorian hymn-writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick William Faber wrote hymns such as 'Faith of Our Fathers'.

clue.text: Drive politician into clumsy lie?

indicators.note: into means the MP goes inside the jumbled letters
clumsy says the letters of lie are awkwardly jumbled

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an MP is pushed into telling an awkward fib.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push forward.

clue.text: DIY outfit sailor brought back for fabric-printing

indicators.note: brought back says the joined pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a kit is a set of parts for self-assembly
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor returns with a self-assembly set for printing designs on cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns KITAB round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is a wax-resist method of dyeing patterns onto cloth.

clue.text: I might start on time — you, I hear, come last, being unprepared

indicators.note: the start of the word might is its first letter

parts.note: on time means prompt or punctual

indicators.note: I hear says the word you is replaced by a letter that sounds like it

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like U

explanation.surface: Someone muses that they may begin punctually while the other person arrives last, without preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come last' tells us U goes at the end; it is a link phrase in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is improvised on the spot, without rehearsal.

clue.text: Set up a ring, to do Ernest a mischief

indicators.note: doing someone a mischief means hurting them, so the letters are knocked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone forms a boxing ring in order to hurt a man named Ernest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up a ring' suggests building a boxing ring, but means made a ringing sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resonated is to have produced a reverberating sound, as a bell does when it rings.

clue.text: Stew that could be made with a sausage

indicators.note: says that adding the letter A would form the sausage, so the sausage's letters cover the answer plus A

parts.note: salami is a spicy Italian sausage

explanation.surface: A cook notes that a stew might be prepared using a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmi is a rich ragout of game birds.
